critical-bundle-gzip.reason: SPEC §21: the user approved a 950 KiB (972,800-byte) operational ceiling on 2026-10-19 for the expanded editor, covers, folder setup and PWA feature set, with a revised 500 KiB (512,000-byte) long-term goal. This is an explicitly approved allowance, not a measured optimized baseline: local main and PR #6 builds with identical dependencies and existing WASM measured 916,381 and 921,198 bytes gzip, respectively, a 4,817-byte increase. The allowance leaves 51,602 bytes (5.6%) above that local candidate; a fresh optimized CI measurement and physical-device acceptance are not claimed. Byte tolerance remains 0%, so one byte above 972,800 fails. Lazy Excalidraw/graph exclusions and all other performance gates remain unchanged.

keystroke-to-paint.reason: SPEC §21.4: the measurement is a double-requestAnimationFrame from keydown and therefore resolves to one 60 Hz frame. It still detects the regression the budget guards against: a keystroke taking multiple frames. Removing this exception requires a reliable sub-frame browser metric.

longest-task.reason: SPEC §21.1: on the 10k perf vault the throttled mobile cold start has several 75-111 ms main-thread tasks (2026-11-09). A CPU profile attributes them to work spread across startup, not one cause: writing the 10,000-note catalog to IndexedDB (putNotes), storing and validating client search segments in WASM (putSearchSegment, mb_search::Segment::postings / validate_postings), and mounting the app. It was 65 ms when first recorded on a smaller setup, and 90 ms on main before Mermaid or inbox paging. Desktop records no task over 50 ms and is deliberately not excepted. Removing it means moving catalog and segment storage off the main thread or chunking it.

graph-fps.reason: SPEC §21.2: the 10,000-node desktop graph measures 58.3 ms p95 under headless Chromium's SwiftShader software renderer; the throttled mobile graph stays inside budget at its 2,000-node cap. Geometry caching improved this from 91.6 ms. Remaining levers are label-pass culling, cached edge rendering, and indexed line buffers.

diagram-longest-task.reason: SPEC §13.2, A38: the user accepted that pages with Mermaid diagrams may miss mid-range Android budgets. Rendering the 43-task Gantt fixture under the 4x throttle produced one 76 ms main-thread task after the editor was ready (Mermaid measures text through the DOM, so it cannot move to a worker). Desktop has no task over 50 ms and is deliberately not excepted. Render time itself is within the Open note budget on both devices (mobile 85.5 ms, desktop 22.2 ms).

diagram-keystroke-to-paint.reason: SPEC §21.4: the same double-requestAnimationFrame resolution as keystroke-to-paint, which is recorded at 16.4 ms desktop and 16.6 ms mobile for the same reason. Mobile measured 15.9, 16.9 and 15.8 ms across runs on 2026-11-08/09: one 60 Hz frame either side of the line. This row is not part of the A38 exception: typing on a diagram page must keep the keystroke budget.

server-memory-idle.reason: SPEC §21.1, §21.11: resident memory after the whole perf run on the 10k vault (debug build, macOS) read 83.7, 277.8 and 412.9 MB on 2026-11-09 with no code change; recorded at the worst. Cause (§21.11): the startup zone-segment rebuild peaked at 233 MB of heap and macOS keeps the freed pages resident, so `ps` RSS tracks machine memory pressure. The rebuild now peaks at 56 MB; RSS during a perf run then read 173-197 MB with a 31-58 MB physical footprint. Lower this entry to the next run's reading; removing it needs the budget decision in §21.11 (measure footprint, or return pages).
